PhD & MFA: Application Fee Waiver (GRS only)
Graduate Information
In an effort to reduce financial barriers to attending graduate school, the central admissions office of the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS) offers application fee waivers to qualifying domestic GRS PhD & MFA applicants.
Please note:
Do not email the Graduate School’s admissions office; instead, follow the instructions below. Do not submit the form found at the bottom of this page and select an incorrect answer on purpose.
The Graduate School’s central admission office does not offer application fee waivers to international applicants (see “International Applicants” below).
If you are a Master’s applicant (incl. MFA in Literary Translation), please visit the Master’s Application Fee Waiver page.
In the “Signature” section of the application, you will be asked for an “Application Access Code.” Please select “No, I don’t have a code.” We do not use application access codes (fee waiver codes) for GRS PhD & MFA applicants. If you qualify, the fee will simply be removed.
GRS PhD & MFA fee waivers can only be used for GRS PhD & MFA programs and only for the current admissions cycle. If your application fee was waived during a previous admissions cycle, you must reapply for a waiver. Non-degree applicants are not eligible for fee waivers.
There are many similar sounding programs at Boston University (ex: Biology, Neurobiology, and Biomedical Engineering are each offered by a different graduate school). You cannot use our Fee Waiver Request Form for a program that we do not offer (ex: Bioinformatics, Neuroscience).
If you are applying to a program that is not offered by Graduate School of Arts and Sciences (GRS), please reach out to the respective schools directly, for example:
⇒ College of Engineering (ENG): Biomedical Engineering, Computer Engineering, etc.
⇒ Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences (CDS): Bioinformatics
⇒ Graduate Medical Sciences (GMS): Biomedical Sciences, Neuroscience, Neurobiology, etc.
⇒ Wheelock College of Education (SED): Counseling Psychology, Social Studies in Education
⇒ Other schools/programs
Application fees cannot be refunded. If you are given a fee waiver, do not submit your application with a payment.
All requests must be received at least five business days prior to the application deadline. Late requests will be denied.
International Applicants
The central admission office of the Graduate School does not offer application fee waivers to international applicants. We do not provide application fee waivers to international applicants based on unfavorable currency exchange rates, currency conversion barriers and fees, low income, family size, unemployment or under-employment, financial hardship, economic or political challenges in their home country, or any other extenuating circumstances. It is not possible to appeal. Please do not email the central admissions office (grsphd@bu.edu, grs@bu.edu), financial aid office (grsaid@bu.edu), or individual staff.
All international applicants must contact their program of interest directly to inquire about the possibility of the department waiving the fee (see “Departmental Recommendation” below). If you have already contacted the program and received no response, please send them a follow up email or call. Do not contact the central admissions office.
When contacting your respective program you must include your full name, email address used in application (it must match the application, the email will be used to find your application in the system, please make sure you check that it is correct and spelled correctly), CV/resume, personal statement, research summary, and copies of your transcripts in your email. If the department determines that you qualify for a fee waiver based on their criteria, the department will contact our admissions office. Please note that not all programs offer application fee waivers.

If the department determines that you qualify for a fee waiver based on their criteria, the department will contact our admissions office. U.S Citizens & U.S. Permanent Residents
If you are a U.S. Citizen or a U.S. Permanent Resident (“Green Card” holder) you may request an application fee waiver based on one of the following criteria:
1. Documented financial hardship
Applicants with current documented financial hardship will be required to provide supporting documentation for at least one of the following, along with a 250+ word (at least half of a single-spaced page) explanation:
A current official statement of your financial need from a financial aid officer at your current institution, which includes your Expected Family Contribution (EFC) or Student Aid Index (SAI), or proof that you received a Pell Grant as an undergraduate student within the past year
A copy of your current FAFSA Student Aid Report (SAR), with your Social Security Number obscured
An official verification of your current participation in a U.S. government low-income aid program, such as Unemployment, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Welfare, Medicaid, etc.
A copy of a waiver granted to you by ETS for GRE fee within the past year
Documents not listing the applicant’s name are not accepted. Do not send copies of tax returns, bank statements, or any document that contains your social security number. Requests that are missing supporting documentation will be denied.
2. First-Generation Applicants
A first generation graduate student is defined as someone whose parents, guardians, or caregivers have not completed an advanced degree, e.g. master’s, doctoral, or professional degree (like a JD or MD). Included in this group are students whose parent(s) have not obtained a four-year degree.
You will need to provide a current copy of your resume along with a 250+ word (at least half of a single-spaced page) statement supporting your request. Requests that are missing supporting documentation will be denied.
3. Military service
Included in this group are U.S. military veterans with Honorable Discharges or those who are on active duty in U.S. Armed Forces. You will need to provide proof of service or discharge. Requests that are missing supporting documentation will be denied.
4. Special Programs, Events, and Fellowships
We are pleased to offer application fee waivers to those who have participated in the following qualified programs, events, and fellowships as a current participant or recent alumni (within the last two years). You will need to provide documentation of your participation or affiliation with your request. Requests that are missing supporting documentation will be denied.

Demonstrates a clear directive for students to enter a doctoral or research program
Is represented or has chapters at more than one U.S. university campus

How to submit your request and next steps
To apply for an application fee waiver, you must first review your eligibility (see above) and have:
1. added your full biographical information to the application, incl. citizenship information
2. uploaded your CV/resume
3. uploaded your personal statement
4. uploaded your research summary (if required)
5. uploaded copies of your transcripts
If you meet any of the criteria, please submit your request via the PhD & MFA Application Fee Waiver Request Form below. Once the submitted information is reviewed and verified (which may take up to five business days), we will waive the application fee for you in the system (no code required). All requests will be reviewed during regular office hours (9am-5pm local time, Monday-Friday), except on holidays and during intersession.
Please note:
In the “Signature” section of the application, you will be asked for an “Application Access Code.” Please select “No, I don’t have a code.” We do not use application access codes (fee waiver codes) for GRS PhD & MFA applicants.
In the “Review” section of the application, you will be asked to click “Finalize Application and Pay.
If your fee waiver request was approved, you will be immediately taken to your Applicant Portal. At the bottom of that page, you will see that the Payment was waived under “Recent Activities.”
Without a fee waiver, a payment screen will pop up asking for credit card information.
